26-qf4-qb-1218.solution: Correlation r = covariance ÷ (σA × σB), so σB = covariance ÷ (r × σA). That gives σB = 30 ÷ (0.6 × 10) = 30 ÷ 6 = 5. So Stock B's volatility is 5.
26-qf4-qb-1218.trick: Covariance ÷ r gives σA × σB: 30 ÷ 0.6 = 50. Then 50 ÷ 10 = 5.

26-qf4-qb-1271.solution: A PIN can start with 0, so the first digit has 10 choices. Digits cannot repeat, so the next three places have 9, 8 and 7 choices. The total is 10P4 = 10 × 9 × 8 × 7 = 5,040.
26-qf4-qb-1271.trick: Do 9 × 8 = 72, then 72 × 7 = 504, then tack on the 0 from the 10 to get 5,040.

26-qf4-qb-1353.solution: Percentile = (number of scores below ÷ total number of scores) × 100. Here that is (75 ÷ 100) × 100 = 75. So the percentile of 82 is 75.
26-qf4-qb-1353.trick: The total is exactly 100, so the number who scored lower is the percentile itself: 75.

26-qf4-qb-1406.solution: Remove the highest value, 18, which leaves 10, 12, 14, 16. The mean is (10 + 12 + 14 + 16) ÷ 4 = 52 ÷ 4 = 13. So the new mean is 13.
26-qf4-qb-1406.trick: The four values are evenly spaced, so the mean is halfway between the ends: (10 + 16) ÷ 2 = 13. Also, the old mean was 14, and dropping the top value must pull it down, so only 13 fits.

26-qf4-qb-1423.solution: The mean of a binomial distribution is np. So the mean is 10 × 0.4 = 4.
26-qf4-qb-1423.trick: np = 10 × 0.4: shift the decimal point one place to get 4.

26-qf4-qb-1462.solution: nC5 = n(n − 1)(n − 2)(n − 3)(n − 4) ÷ 120. For n = 10 this is 30,240 ÷ 120 = 252, and nC5 only gets bigger as n grows. So n = 10.
26-qf4-qb-1462.trick: Test the smallest option and cancel: 10C5 = (10 ÷ 5) × (8 ÷ 4) × (9 ÷ 3) × (6 ÷ 2) × 7 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 7 = 252. Options 20 and 40 would give far bigger numbers.

26-qf4-qb-1497.solution: Product A sold double the units of Product B. So A sold 2 × 50 = 100 units.

26-qf4-qb-1512.solution: Choose the boys and the girls separately, then multiply. 7C3 = (7 × 6 × 5) ÷ 6 = 35 and 5C2 = (5 × 4) ÷ 2 = 10. So the number of ways is 35 × 10 = 350.
26-qf4-qb-1512.trick: 7C3 = 35 and 5C2 = 10, so 35 × 10 = 350. The answer must be a multiple of 7, and only 350 is.

26-qf4-qb-1523.solution: A full circle is 360°, which is 100%. So 72° is (72 ÷ 360) × 100% = 20%.
26-qf4-qb-1523.trick: 72 × 5 = 360, so the sector is one fifth of the circle, which is 20%.

26-qf4-qb-1530.solution: A few high scores pull the mean above the median. Here the mean (70) is above the median (65), which points to a long tail on the right. So the distribution is positively skewed.
26-qf4-qb-1530.trick: The mean chases the tail. Mean above median means positive skew.

26-qf4-qb-1571.solution: Mean = sum ÷ number of values = (10 + 14 + 16 + 20 + 30) ÷ 5 = 90 ÷ 5 = 18. So the mean is 18.
26-qf4-qb-1571.trick: Measure from 20: the gaps are −10, −6, −4, 0 and +10, which add to −10. Then −10 ÷ 5 = −2, so the mean is 20 − 2 = 18.

26-qf4-qb-1599.solution: Range = maximum − minimum, so maximum = range + minimum = 50 + 15 = 65.
26-qf4-qb-1599.trick: Add the range to the minimum: 15 + 50 = 65.

26-qf4-qb-1639.solution: Arrange the scores in order: 12, 15, 18, 20, 22. With 5 scores, the median is the middle (third) one. So the median is 18.
26-qf4-qb-1639.trick: Find the score with two below it and two above it: 18 has 12 and 15 below, and 20 and 22 above.

26-qf4-qb-1647.solution: Using Pearson's second coefficient, skewness = 3 × (mean − median) ÷ SD. So 0.9 = 3 × (50 − 41) ÷ SD = 27 ÷ SD. Then SD = 27 ÷ 0.9 = 30.

26-qf4-bm-2469.solution: A sample is a smaller group drawn from the population. Data means recorded values and a distribution describes how values are spread, so neither is a group taken from the population. The answer is Sample.
26-qf4-bm-2469.trick: Only a sample is a smaller group picked out of a population. Pick Sample.

26-qf4-bm-2473.solution: For a Poisson distribution, the variance is equal to the mean. So if the mean is m, the variance is m.
26-qf4-bm-2473.trick: Remember: Poisson, mean equals variance. Pick m.

26-qf4-bm-2477.solution: Taking $100 as the mean rent and $150 as the standard deviation, the rent 2 standard deviations above the mean is mean + 2 × SD. That is $100 + 2 × $150 = $100 + $300 = $400.
26-qf4-bm-2477.trick: Double the SD: 2 × 150 = 300. Add the mean: 300 + 100 = 400.

26-qf4-bm-2484.solution: The order does not matter, so use 20C4 = (20 × 19 × 18 × 17) ÷ (4 × 3 × 2 × 1) = 116,280 ÷ 24 = 4,845. So the number of committees is 4,845.
26-qf4-bm-2484.trick: Cancel first: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 and 18 ÷ 6 = 3, leaving 5 × 3 × 19 × 17. Every factor is odd, so the answer is odd, and only 4,845 is odd.

26-qf4-bm-2491.solution: The correlation coefficient r always lies between −1 and +1. A perfect inverse (negative) relationship gives r = −1.
26-qf4-bm-2491.trick: Inverse means negative, and perfect means the extreme end, so r = −1. Values like 2 and 4 are impossible because r never goes beyond ±1.

26-qf4-bm-2496.solution: A full circle is 360°, which is 100%. So 36° is (36 ÷ 360) × 100% = 10%.
26-qf4-bm-2496.trick: 36° is one tenth of 360°, so it is 10%.

26-qf4-bm-2501.solution: A confidence interval for a mean is the sample mean ± a margin of error, so the mean is the midpoint of the interval. The midpoint is (45 + 55) ÷ 2 = 50. So the sample mean is 50.
26-qf4-bm-2501.trick: The mean sits in the exact middle of the interval, halfway between 45 and 55, which is 50.

26-qf4-bm-2506.solution: Variance measures how far the observations spread around the mean. It is 0 only when there is no spread at all, which happens when every observation has the same value. So the answer is Same.
26-qf4-bm-2506.trick: No spread at all means every value is identical. Pick Same.

26-qf4-bm-2511.trick: 40 − 20 is 20, so 40 − 21 is one less: 19. The 20 option is the trap.

26-qf4-bm-2516.solution: Two dice give 36 equally likely outcomes. A product above 25 happens only for (5, 6), (6, 5) and (6, 6), which is 3 outcomes, because 5 × 5 = 25 is not above 25. So the probability is 3 ÷ 36 = 1/12.
26-qf4-bm-2516.trick: Only a 5 with a 6, or two 6s, beats 25. That is 3 pairs out of 36, so 3/36 = 1/12. Remember that 5 × 5 = 25 does not count.

26-qf4-bm-2523.solution: After a white is drawn first, 6 remain: 3 red and 3 white. So P(second is red) = 3 ÷ 6 = 1/2.
26-qf4-bm-2523.trick: Take out one white: 3 red and 3 white are left, an even split, so 1/2.

26-qf4-bm-2529.solution: The final cumulative frequency is the total number of observations. There are 4 values, so the running totals are 1, 2, 3, 4. The final cumulative frequency is 4.
26-qf4-bm-2529.trick: The last cumulative frequency always equals the number of observations. Count the values: 4.

26-qf4-bm-2534.solution: In a perfectly symmetrical distribution with one peak, the centre is the mean, the median and the mode all at once. So the three are equal.
26-qf4-bm-2534.trick: Symmetric means no skew, so the mean, median and mode sit at the same point. Pick Equal.

26-qf4-bm-2537.solution: A boxplot is drawn from the five number summary: minimum, Q1, median, Q3 and maximum. The length of the box gives the IQR (Q3 − Q1) and the line inside the box is the median. A standard boxplot does not show the mean, so the answer is Mean.
26-qf4-bm-2537.trick: A boxplot is built from the five number summary: minimum, Q1, median, Q3 and maximum. The mean is not one of them.

26-qf4-bm-2541.solution: Arrange the times in order: 8, 10, 12, 14, 20. With 5 values, the median is the middle (third) one. So the median wait time is 12.
26-qf4-bm-2541.trick: Cross off the smallest and largest (8 and 20), then do it again (10 and 14). The one left is 12.

26-qf4-bm-2546.solution: An ER (entity relationship) diagram is used to model how data is structured: the entities, their attributes and the relationships between them. A pie chart and a box plot are used to display data, not to model it. So the answer is ER Diagram.
26-qf4-bm-2546.trick: ER means entity relationship, which is about how data is structured. A pie chart and a box plot are charts for showing data. Pick ER Diagram.

26-qf4-bm-2549.solution: List the pairs with a sum of 8: (2, 6), (3, 5), (4, 4), (5, 3), (6, 2). So the number of outcomes is 5.
26-qf4-bm-2549.trick: With two dice, a sum of 7 has the most ways (6). Each step away from 7 loses one way, so a sum of 8 has 5.

26-qf4-bm-2556.solution: A parameter is a measure that describes a characteristic of a whole population, such as the population mean. A sample is only part of the population, and a variable is what is measured on each member. So the answer is Parameter.
26-qf4-bm-2556.trick: Parameter goes with Population, and statistic goes with Sample. Pick Parameter.
